newsitem.title: PERU: Peru court rejects bid to stop Fujimori reelection.
newsitem.headline: Peru court rejects bid to stop Fujimori reelection.

text.p: Peru's highest court for constitutional matters rejected on Thursday a move to block President Alberto Fujimori from running for a third term in 2000.

The Constitutional Court threw out a petition from the Lima Chamber of Lawyers that a Congressional ruling be declared "inapplicable" that interpreted the constitution in such a way as to allow Fujimori to stand for reelection.
A court statement said the petition had been judged "unfounded" due to the abstention of four of the court's seven voting magistrates. Six votes are needed for a decision.
The ruling reinforces Fujimori's position, allowing him to plan a fresh election bid for 2000 if he wants to.

Under Peruvian law a president who has been elected for two consecutive terms, as is Fujimori's case, cannot run in the next election. But Congress voted in August in favour of a legal interpretation that meant Fujimori's first term would not be taken into account if he wished to stand again.

Fujimori was elected president in 1990 and again in 1995 with 64 percent of the vote. After he dissolved parliament during his 1992 "self-coup," a new constitution was written the following year by a reformulated Congress, paving the way for the interpretation accepted in August.

The Constitutional Court's decision came as Fujimori faced the toughest test of his six years in office, with Marxist rebels holding 74 VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for the 30th day.
The president has not formally announced an intention to run again in 2000, but has reportedly said privately that he wants to.
